newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end little changed, eye on jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end little changed, eye on jobs data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in quiet trade on Thursday, with many investors taking a cautious stance ahead of the release tomorrow of key U.S. and Canadian jobs data, analysts said.

"(Investors) are just trying to get themselves squared off ahead of tomorrow's (U.S.) employment number. That is a key number. It is the only employment number that the Fed will see before the next FOMC meeting," said David Yu, a fixed-income porfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.16 to C$112.38 to yield 7.006 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.88 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 13 basis points from 14 basis points on Wednesday.
Statistics Canada on Friday will release the country's employment report for May, while the United States will release its non-farm payrolls report for the same month.

Fixed-income investors will study the employment reports for evidence of inflation growth in both countries, and clues about whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike U.S. interest rates when its Open Market Committee meets in July, analysts said.

Analysts said the only significant activity in the Canadian market was the rebound in real return bonds following the poorly-received auction of C$500 million in 4.25 percent real return bonds due 2026 on Wednesday.
Canada's 4.25 percent real return bond due December 1, 2021 ended the session up C$0.35 to C$98.60 to yield 4.343 percent.

Among new issues, the Government of Canada said it plans to auction on June 11 C$3.5 billion of bonds with an unspecified coupon and maturing on September 15, 1999. The Bank of Canada will buy at least C$350 million of the bonds.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.14 to C$105.56 to yield 6.484 percent while the U.S. 10-year rose 2/32 to 6.62 percent.
The negative spread widened to 14 basis points from 11 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.89 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.10 percent.
